title: Investment appraisal
examples: How do I decide which project to choose?
What is the difference between payback and NPV?
Can you explain the time value of money again?

explain.say: The first method is the payback period. It tells us how quickly we get our money back.

items: Annual Cash Flow: Money earned each year
Payback Period: Time to recover initial cost

draw.text: Payback Period: Time to recover investment

explain.say: To calculate it, we divide the initial cost by the annual cash flow. This gives us the payback time.

draw.text: Payback = Initial Cost / Annual Cash Flow

explain.say: Next we look at the Accounting Rate of Return. This measures profitability using accounting profit. It is a percentage.
The final method is Net Present Value. This accounts for the time value of money using a discount rate.

draw.text: NPV: Value today of future cash flows

explain.say: Consider buying a new machine costing one hundred thousand pounds. It earns twenty thousand pounds yearly for five years. Calculate the payback.
A real-life example is choosing between two delivery routes for your business. One route pays back quickly but earns less overall profit. The other earns more but takes longer to pay back.

faq.q: What is the time value of money in investment appraisal?
faq.a: It means that money received today is worth more than the same amount received in the future. This is because you can invest the money today and earn interest.
asks: Why is money today worth more?
How does time affect money value?

faq.q: Should I always use Net Present Value?
faq.a: No, NPV is very useful, but sometimes payback period is preferred if the company is in urgent cash flow trouble. Each method has different strengths.
asks: Is NPV always the best measure?
When should I ignore the payback period?

faq.q: Does ARR use after-tax profit or before-tax profit?
faq.a: ARR calculations should generally use the after-tax profit figure. This reflects the actual profit the business keeps after paying taxes.
asks: Which profit figure should I use for ARR?
Does tax affect the ARR calculation?

faq.q: What is the main weakness of the payback period?
faq.a: Its main weakness is that it ignores all cash flows that occur after the payback period. It only looks at the recovery time.
asks: Is ignoring future cash flows okay?

faq.q: How is the discount rate used in NPV?
faq.a: The discount rate represents the required rate of return or the cost of capital for the business. It discounts future cash flows back to their present value.

facts: The payback period calculates the time needed to recoup the initial investment.
ARR uses accounting profit to measure profitability relative to investment.
NPV accounts for the time value of money using a discount rate.
A shorter payback period is generally preferred by risk-averse investors.

quiz.say: A project costs one hundred thousand pounds and generates twenty thousand pounds profit each year. What is the payback period?
quiz.why: Dividing the total cost by the annual cash flow correctly shows the recovery time.

wrong.0: Dividing the cash flow by the cost is the reverse calculation.
wrong.2: Multiplying the cost by the cash flow is incorrect for finding time.
wrong.3: This is just the annual cash flow, not the time taken.

quiz.say: If a business expects a profit of thirty thousand pounds on a one hundred thousand pound investment, what is the ARR?
quiz.why: The formula for ARR is profit divided by the initial investment, shown as a percentage.

wrong.0: Adding the profit and investment is incorrect for this ratio.
wrong.1: This assumes no profit, ignoring the given profit figure.
wrong.3: Adding the profit and investment is not part of the ARR formula.

quiz.say: Which method best reflects that money received later is worth less?
quiz.why: NPV explicitly uses a discount rate to adjust future cash flows to today's value.

wrong.0: This ignores the concept of opportunity cost over time.
wrong.2: Payback ignores the timing and value of cash flows after recovery.
wrong.3: ARR only uses accounting profit and does not discount future earnings.
